title: Oregon's 3rd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Oregon's 3rd Congressional District, covering most of Multnomah County, northeastern Clackamas County, and all of Hood River County, is holding its general election on November 3, 2026. The district is the most Democratic congressional district in Oregon, rated "Solid D" or "Safe D" by all major nonpartisan election forecasters. Incumbent Democrat Maxine Dexter, a physician and former state representative who first won the seat in 2024, faces Republican nominee Loran Ayles, who won his party's primary unopposed. The race presents voters with a clear contrast between Dexter's progressive record on healthcare, housing, and environmental issues, and Ayles' background as an activist opposed to COVID-19 restrictions.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race. The district is considered safely Democratic by major forecasters including Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball, all of which rate it as Solid/Safe Democratic.

candidates.name: Maxine Dexter
candidates.summary: Maxine Dexter is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Oregon's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. She is a physician (pulmonologist and critical care specialist) who previously served in the Oregon House of Representatives, where she chaired the House Housing and Homelessness Committee and led efforts on healthcare access, abortion rights, and homelessness funding. In Congress, she serves on the House Veterans' Affairs and Natural Resources Committees.

candidates.name: Loran Ayles
candidates.summary: Loran Ayles is the Republican nominee for Oregon's 3rd Congressional District. He advanced from the Republican primary unopposed. Ayles was previously involved with Open Our Oregon, a group that sued to challenge COVID-19 restriction measures. He has a prior misdemeanor conviction for identity theft related to a 2013 incident that emerged during a 2019 school board campaign. Limited public biographical information is available about his professional background.

forecast.rationale: No public polls are available for this race, but Oregon's 3rd Congressional District is the most Democratic district in Oregon and is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by all major nonpartisan forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball). Incumbent Democrat Maxine Dexter, a physician and former state representative who won the seat in 2024, has the advantages of incumbency, a well-established political profile, and represents a district that consistently delivers large Democratic margins (Blumenauer's 2022 margin was ~35 points). Republican nominee Loran Ayles advanced unopposed in his primary but has limited public biographical information, a thin professional profile, and a prior misdemeanor identity theft conviction. Given the deep Democratic lean of the district and the contrast in candidate profiles, a Democratic hold is virtually certain. The lack of polling does not materially reduce confidence here because the structural partisan fundamentals are overwhelming and well-documented across multiple independent rating sources.
